name: Orchid Pink
lede: Orchid Pink is a soft, light pink with a hint of purple, named for the flower and easy to confuse with the much stronger web color Orchid.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines orchid pink as a lightish pink, sometimes a deep pink or a purplish pink [1]. His own range shows the name was loose [1]. The library's swatch is the pale end: ISCC-NBS block 2 calls it a "light purplish pink", and Ridgway's 1912 atlas and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary both carry it [2].

Do not mix it up with [[orchid]]. Paterson notes that Orchid in the X11 set is hex #DA70D6, a vivid magenta-violet, far stronger than this swatch [1]. Orchid pink sits among the soft pinks: closest to [[pale-pink]] and [[pink]], with [[lilac]] on its cooler side [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Orchid pink is almost absent from painting. Only 3 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive carry it over at least five per cent of the canvas, as photographed, which is rarer than 86 per cent of the named colors [3]. Light pinks this delicate are easy to lose in aged, varnished paintings, so the count says more about the photographs than about the painters [3].
